title: We Learn to Give, Share and Care
description: Attitudes and values, and the language of philanthropy: the vocabulary of giving (philanthropy, altruism, activism, volunteerism, charity, donation, self-sacrifice, generosity, solidarity, endowment, fund-raising, benevolence, welfare, the needy, in-kind contributions); agent nouns in -er, -or and -ist, which name the person from the act (donor, endower, fund-raiser, philanthropist, activist, altruist, volunteer) and the beneficiary who receives; compound adjectives built with a hyphen in front of the noun (a fund-raising concert, a well-run charity, ever-increasing costs, state-of-the-art equipment); the emphatic form do, does and did before the base verb of an affirmative simple present or simple past, and the auxiliary that takes the stress instead when there already is one; need as an ordinary full verb, before a noun and before a to-infinitive; the phrasal verbs of the module (care for, give up, grow up, catch up with, win over, stay up, come round, take over, gossip about, bring out) with the separable and inseparable ones and the place of a pronoun; should have plus a past participle for the sensible action that did not happen; the central contrast of the year, the present perfect against the simple past, with its four uses, the finished time-periods that refuse it, the markers that call each tense and the rule that since plus a starting point opens a period reaching today; the other simple past, the one that is not about the past, after if, suppose, as if, if only, it's high time, would rather and wish; the shape of a speech that persuades, its four ways of catching an audience and its counterargument move; and the discourse markers that show the joints of a text
